hints: Focus on the first step of electrophilic addition, where the double bond in propene attacks the H in HBr.
Adding H+ to the end carbon gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}^+\text{CH}_3$, while adding it to the middle carbon gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2^+$ .
Remember that the more stable carbocation forms faster and in much larger amount, so compare secondary versus primary stability.
walkthrough:
**Spot the mechanism type**

Addition of HBr to an alkene is electrophilic addition. The pi bond acts as a nucleophile and takes $\text{H}^+$ from HBr first.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{carbocation intermediate} + \text{Br}^-$$

**Draw the two possible carbocations**

H can join to either end of the double bond. This gives two different positive ions.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}^+\text{CH}_3 \text{ (secondary)}$$ 
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2^+ \text{ (primary)}$$

**Pick the more stable ion**

Carbocations are stabilised by neighbouring alkyl groups through inductive donation and hyperconjugation. A secondary carbocation with two methyl groups is much more stable than a primary one with only one ethyl group.

So the secondary ion $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}^+\text{CH}_3$ forms faster and in the greatest amount, leading to the Markovnikov major product $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3$.

options.A: This is the secondary carbocation $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}^+\text{CH}_3$. It is stabilised by two electron donating methyl groups, so it is lower in energy and forms in greatest amount. Attack by $\text{Br}^-$ then gives 2-bromopropane, the Markovnikov product.
options.B: This is the primary carbocation $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2^+$. It has only one alkyl group to stabilise the positive charge, so it is much less stable and forms only in tiny amount as the minor pathway.
options.C: This shows a carbanion ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}^-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) with a negative charge. Electrophilic addition of HBr goes via positive carbocations, not negative carbanions, and Br- adds in the second fast step, not the first.
options.D: This is also a carbanion ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2^-$). Students sometimes confuse electrophile and nucleophile roles, but the alkene accepts $\text{H}^+$, so the intermediate must be positive, never negative like this.
